target_state: implemented in staging. The whole 450-instruction body was re-derived from the image bytes for this package: the frame, all fifteen key ids, the twenty-three receiver displacements, the three slot displacements of the parameter object, the two data addresses, the one direct callee's own 0x61 bytes, and the 0.0f / the two reciprocals read out of .rdata and .data. The Ghidra decompilation was used only as a hint and is contradicted by the listing in three places, each resolved in favour of the listing (see mechanics.decompiler_disagreements). The 12-fold repeated block is modelled by one helper and the model test checks that factorisation against an instruction-by-instruction transcription of one of the copies. Nothing is claimed about the class, about the meaning of any key id, about the twenty-one float displacements as a layout, or about the class of the record.

implementation.argument_surface: the hidden receiver in ECX, aliased into ESI at 0x005a2603 and reached only through that alias; no ordinary stack argument. The frame is three pushes and no SUB ESP, so ESP is entry-12 throughout, and all five terminators are POP ESI / POP EBX / POP ECX / RET, i.e. caller-owned cleanup of zero bytes. The body is a zero-parameter member, so the ordinary stack argument count is zero and the record's own abi_derived.stack_arguments (observed_slots 0, derived_slots 0, total_bytes 0) agrees.
implementation.return_type_note: The listing produces no value on any of its five terminators: every x87 load is consumed by the FSTP two instructions later, every XMM0 is consumed by a store to memory, and the last four terminators are each reached straight from a store into the receiver. The declared void therefore rests on the bytes, and it is the value this sidecar records in observed_original_abi.return_type, which is the canonical layer the RETURN SEMANTICS check compares the source against. It is NOT the same as the pack's derived abi envelope, which reports return_register ST0 and return_semantics float_or_x87_in_ST0 on the strength of inference RT1 at confidence APPROXIMATION ('an x87 or SSE instruction appears in the body'). This body is a counterexample to that inference: it contains twenty-three FPU instructions and returns nothing. The disagreement is recorded, not hidden, and no typedef named after the record's phrase was created to make the two strings compare equal. See return_semantics.record_disagreement and unresolved_questions item 1.
implementation.receiver_model: an opaque byte run with NO named members. The machine-derived receiver record is bounds_only, so naming a member would assert an identity no evidence in this pack can confirm; every receiver, object and record access goes through a displacement accessor instead, which is also what makes a wrong displacement in the .cpp land on a decoy byte in the model test rather than on a plausible-looking field.
implementation.dispatch_model: three slots of the object the receiver holds at its +0x10, at displacements 0x1c, 0x24 and 0x28, declared as three named extern callees with the receiver in ECX and callee-owned cleanup. The class is not named by any record, so nothing else about it is declared. The class THIS body belongs to is a different matter and is deliberately NOT modelled: the image places 0x005a2600 at slot +0x64 of the table whose head is 0x013f69b4 (the word at 0x013f6a18 is 0x005a2600), but the body never reads its own leading word as a table word, so no slot is declared for it.
implementation.dependency_note: the one direct callee 0x0041ea70 and the three slot callees are declared extern in the package header and defined as observers in the package's own model test; no other package's header is included. 0x0041ea70 is named with the repository's own name for it, unresolved_0041ea70, taken from reconstruction/staging/pkg-palette-wave11/pkg_palette_wave11.hpp line 377, so this package does not invent a competing one.

observed_mechanics: the frame is PUSH ECX / PUSH EBX / PUSH ESI with no SUB ESP, so ESP is entry-12 for the whole body and every terminator restores it with POP ESI / POP EBX / POP ECX

0x005a2603 MOV ESI,ECX aliases the receiver into ESI and every receiver access in the body goes through that alias, which is why the machine-derived receiver record reports register ECX with shape R-ALIAS and a literal scan of ECX's own operands finds nothing

the one stack slot the body ever addresses is [ESP+0x8] == entry-4, which is exactly the word 0x005a2600's PUSH ECX filled: it is taken by address at 0x005a2a34 and 0x005a2a65 and read back at 0x005a2a44 and 0x005a2a75, so both +0x24 callees are handed the same out-parameter and the second overwrites the first
the receiver's +0x10 word is read seventeen times and is the only receiver displacement the body reads
the receiver's +0x9c byte is cleared once, at 0x005a2608, before any other receiver access, and nothing in the body ever sets it
twenty-one 4-byte float stores go to twenty-one distinct receiver displacements, 0x14 through 0x70 with 0x2c and 0x74+ absent from the set
BL is loaded with 0x30 at 0x005a261b and is the mask of all twelve TEST BYTE PTR [EAX+0x10],BL instructions; the record-reading idiom therefore tests the BYTE at the record's +0x10, not the word
twenty-six of the twenty-eight indirect transfers read one of three displacements off the object's first word: fourteen at 0x1c, twelve at 0x28 and two at 0x24
each of the twelve inline blocks loads the receiver's +0x10 word twice, once for the +0x1c slot and once for the +0x28 slot, and no copy of it is cached across a block

the two +0x24 blocks null-check the parameter object (TEST ECX,ECX / JZ) and the last block does not, so the check is local to those two blocks and is in fact unreachable in the machine, which faults at 0x005a260f before it
the two +0x24 blocks accept the type tag 0xd alone, while the twelve inline blocks accept 0xd or 0x10
the last block's fallback stores 0x013f6964 itself (0x005a2b10 MOVSS XMM0,dword ptr [0x013f6964]), not a scaled zero and not the record's value

five blocks load through x87 (FLD/FSTP: keys 0x00c7c4f8, 0x00c7c4fa, 0x00c7c4f9, 0x00fe23b2, 0x00fe2437) and seven through SSE (MOVSS), which is register selection and not a semantic difference: every load is 32 bits out of memory and every store is 32 bits to memory
the 0x0041ea70 call sites pass their argument in ECX with no register reload, so the callee receives the record that 0x005a2a44 / 0x005a2a75 read back out of the frame word

mechanics.body_shape: clear one receiver byte, then run fifteen key-id blocks against the parameter object the receiver holds at its +0x10. Twelve blocks ask the object's +0x1c slot whether the key is present and, if it is, ask its +0x28 slot for the record, then read one float out of that record under the tag-and-flag rules and store it at one or two of the receiver's own displacements. Two blocks instead ask the +0x24 slot for a record through an out-parameter in the frame, insist its type word is exactly 0xd, and get the float from this body's one direct callee. The fifteenth block is the twelfth's shape with a multiply by the other reciprocal and a fallback that stores the multiplier itself.

frame_resolution.method: one linear walk of ESP through all 450 instructions, using each callee's own terminator to settle the stack after every call. Entry ESP is 0 in the walk; three pushes take it to -12 and it is -12 for the whole body apart from the two +0x24 call sites, where two pushes take it to -20 and the callee's own RET 8 brings it back to -12. The five terminators each pop three words and return, landing on entry ESP with the return address still on top of the caller's frame: the frame balances exactly.
frame_resolution.corroboration: two independent agreements. (1) The only [ESP+disp] the body forms is [ESP+0x8] at 0x005a2a34, 0x005a2a44, 0x005a2a65 and 0x005a2a75. At ESP = entry-12 that is entry-4, which is exactly where 0x005a2600's PUSH ECX put the incoming receiver, and the epilogue's POP ECX reads that same word. (2) Nothing in the body adjusts ESP: a search of the complete listing finds no ADD ESP, no SUB ESP after the prologue, no LEA ESP and no MOV EBP,ESP, so the only way the frame can balance at five separate terminators is if every callee cleans up after itself, which is what the two +0x24 pushes require.

slots.entry-4: the word PUSH ECX filled. Doubles as the out-parameter of both +0x24 calls, and is read back as the record address at 0x005a2a44 and 0x005a2a75. POP ECX at each terminator restores whatever is there, so on the paths that took those blocks ECX does not come back holding the receiver.

frame_resolution.not_modelled: the clobbering of the saved receiver word, and the value ECX holds at each terminator. Both are unobservable to this body's callers and neither is asserted.

receiver_displacement.0x10: read seventeen times, first at 0x005a2605 (MOV ECX,[ESI+0x10]). It is the parameter object every one of the fifteen blocks goes through, and no block caches it.
receiver_displacement.0x9c: written once, at 0x005a2608 (MOV BYTE PTR [ESI+0x9c],0x0), before any other receiver access
receiver_displacement.0x70: written at 0x005a2acd, 0x005a2ae9, 0x005a2b07 and 0x005a2b18 (MOVSS) by key 0x044c6220, and it is the only displacement with four distinct store sites

mechanics.receiver_record_agreement: the machine-derived receiver record enumerates exactly twenty-three displacements -- 0x10, 0x14, 0x18, 0x1c, 0x28, 0x30, 0x34, 0x38, 0x3c, 0x40, 0x44, 0x48, 0x4c, 0x50, 0x54, 0x58, 0x5c, 0x60, 0x64, 0x68, 0x6c, 0x70, 0x9c -- which is the set above, one read and twenty-two writes, with 0x14 through 0x70 as twenty-one float stores and 0x9c as the one byte store. The record's written_through is 18, which is a lower bound on the twenty-two writes (it counts only the writes it saw through one alias path); the displacement SET agrees exactly and that is what this package relies on. bounds_only is true, so no member is named anywhere in the package.
mechanics.displacement_observation_not_claimed: ten of the twenty-one float displacements come in pairs a fixed 0x14 apart (0x34/0x48, 0x30/0x44, 0x3c/0x50, 0x40/0x54, and 0x28/0x3c/0x40 for the two keys that write the other members of those runs), and one key writes three of them. That is consistent with two or three parallel runs of floats in the object, and it is reported here as an observation only: no record in this repository says so, no member is named for any of the twenty-one, and the model groups nothing. See unresolved_questions item 4.

mechanics.record_reading_grammar: four cases, fixed by the twelve identical copies. type = word at +0x12; flag = byte at +0x10. If type is 0xd or 0x10 and flag & 0x30 is set, the value is the float at the address in the record's leading word. If type is 0xd or 0x10 and flag & 0x30 is clear, the value is the float in the record's leading word. Otherwise, and for every other type, the value is the float at 0x015d1168, which the image shows to be 0.0f. The fourth case of the machine -- type zero with the flag clear, which 0x0041ea74 would answer with NULL -- is unreachable from this body, because the copy is only reached with a type of 0xd or 0x10, and the model says so in a comment rather than reproducing the fault.
mechanics.control_flow: fifty-eight conditional branches and twelve unconditional jumps, all with targets inside the recovered body span 0x005a2600..0x005a2b20, which the validator's own branch closure confirms (no escaping target, no unbounded target). The conditional branches are: twenty-one TEST AL,AL / JZ pairs that gate the fifteen blocks (twelve plus the last, and the two +0x24 blocks have one each, so twenty-one in all); twenty-four CMP CX,0xd / JZ and CMP CX,0x10 / JZ pairs plus their TEST byte / JZ follow-ons that pick the record's arm; two CMP WORD PTR [ECX+0x12],0xd / JNZ tests in the +0x24 blocks; two TEST ECX,ECX / JZ null checks; and the remainder that fall out of those. Every one of them is a local decision inside a single block: no branch leaves the body and no block shares code with another.
mechanics.intra_procedural_jumps: twelve JMP instructions, at 0x005a2645, 0x005a264e, 0x005a2695, 0x005a269e, 0x005a26e5, 0x005a26ee, 0x005a2735, 0x005a273e, 0x005a27a7's predecessors and the rest, all of the form JMP <the FLD or MOVSS that consumes the selected base>. They target 0x005a2659, 0x005a26a9, 0x005a26f9, 0x005a2749, 0x005a27a7, 0x005a2808, 0x005a2869, 0x005a28c2, 0x005a291b, 0x005a296b, 0x005a29bb and 0x005a2a17, all inside the body. They are the tail of the record-reading idiom, not transfers out of it, and the validator's own call comparison excludes them.
mechanics.block_order: the fifteen blocks run in the listing's order and each is independent of the others except through the shared frame word at [ESP+0x8], which only the two +0x24 blocks touch. The order is therefore not load-bearing for any value this body produces, and it is kept because the listing fixes it. The model test asserts it anyway, by checking the order of the calls in the observer's trace.

mechanics.decompiler_disagreements: the live decompilation is used as a hint and is contradicted by the listing in three places, each resolved in favour of the listing. (1) It heads the function __fastcall and models param_1 as an ordinary int, while the terminators are bare RETs and the receiver is an ECX value aliased at 0x005a2603. (2) It reports the two 0x6fda2e1c and 0x8fda2e23 blocks as reading `*(undefined4 *)(param_1 + 0x3c)` from an undefined4 rather than as a scaled read, and it renders the five x87 blocks with FLD/FSTP and the seven SSE blocks with MOVSS/MULSS in a way that makes the last block look like it returns from three places; the listing has one multiply per scaled block and four exits from the last. (3) It spells the mask test as `(*(byte *)(puVar5 + 4) & 0x30)`, i.e. it puts the flag byte at the record's +0x10 and the value at the record's +0x00 in the same words this package uses, but it renders the else arm of the tag test as `puVar5 = &DAT_015d1168` for EVERY unaccepted type including a type of zero, whereas the listing's MOVZX/NEG/SBB/AND arm yields the record for any non-zero type and the 0x015d1168 fallback is reached only from the tag comparisons.

mechanics.not_modelled: the object's class and its three slot implementations; the meaning of the fifteen key ids; any grouping of the twenty-one float displacements; the class this body belongs to and its slot in the table at 0x013f69b4; the meaning of the byte at the receiver's +0x9c; the value of EAX, XMM0 or ECX at any terminator; and the clobbering of the saved receiver word at [ESP+0x8].

return_semantics.value: no value is produced. Every x87 load is consumed by the FSTP two instructions later, every XMM0 is consumed by a store into the receiver, and the four terminators of the last block are each reached immediately after a store into the receiver at +0x70.
return_semantics.ownership: the body performs no reference acquisition or release of its own. It reads a pointer to the parameter object and hands addresses to three slots and one out-of-line helper; whether that object is owned, borrowed or a smart handle is not established by any record for this target and is not claimed.
return_semantics.lifetime: the only object with a lifetime inside this body is the record the +0x24 callees hand back through the frame word at [ESP+0x8]. That word is reused by the second call, so the first record's only remaining use is the FLD inside the first block. Whether either record is owned by the callee, by the parameter object, or by the caller is not established here.
return_semantics.record_disagreement: The pack's derived abi envelope reports return_register ST0 and return_semantics float_or_x87_in_ST0, on the strength of inference RT1 at confidence APPROXIMATION, whose claim is 'an x87 or SSE instruction appears in the body'. The listing refutes that inference for this body: all five terminators are reached with no value in any return register, every FLD is consumed by an FSTP two instructions later, and every MOVSS into XMM0 is consumed by a store. The model declares void, and so does observed_original_abi.return_type in this sidecar, which is why RETURN SEMANTICS passes. The derived envelope's phrase is NOT adopted and no typedef named after it was invented: it is a machine-vocabulary phrase, not a C type, and adopting it would be a false claim about the body.

indirect_transfers.note: all 28 read one of three displacements off the object's first word and are entered as CALL EDX or CALL EAX. The validator's own classifier reads all 28 as VTABLE_SLOT with exactly those three slot displacements, and abi_derived.dispatch counts 28 indirect calls, so the two machine sources agree.

unresolved_questions: The pack's derived ABI envelope and the listing disagree about this body's return value, and the disagreement survives the validation. The envelope says return_register ST0 and return_semantics float_or_x87_in_ST0; the body returns nothing on any of its five terminators. The model declares void, and RETURN SEMANTICS passes only because the canonical claim is the persisted ABI layer -- the one this sidecar declares -- and that layer carries return_type 'void'. The envelope's inference behind its own claim is RT1 at confidence APPROXIMATION, 'an x87 or SSE instruction appears in the body', which is a statement about the body containing an FPU instruction and not about what it returns; this body contains twenty-three FPU instructions and returns nothing, so it is a counterexample to that inference. Whether the inference should be narrowed for bodies of this shape is not established here, and no typedef named after the envelope's phrase was invented to make two strings compare equal.

The two +0x24 blocks null-check the parameter object (0x005a2a2b, 0x005a2a5c) and the other thirteen blocks do not. Which of the two is not established, and the model reproduces them because the bytes are there.

What 0x0041ea70 is FOR is not established. It takes a record in ECX, applies the same tag-and-flag rules as this body's twelve inline copies, and returns a pointer to a float; it is called exactly twice, both times after a +0x24 lookup whose answer is true and whose record's type word is 0xd. The repository's name for it is unresolved_0041ea70, which is itself an admission that no record identifies it. It is a global-ish accessor of some kind (its body contains no reference to a receiver beyond ECX and no reference to any global), but what it selects is unknown.

The twenty-one float displacements are not grouped into anything. Ten of them come in pairs a fixed 0x14 apart and one key writes three, which is consistent with two or three parallel float runs in the object, and no record in this repository establishes that. If the integrator can confirm a layout, the twenty-one constants in the header are the place to attach it; nothing in the model depends on a grouping.

The meaning of the byte the receiver clears at its +0x9c is unknown. It is cleared once, on entry, before any other receiver access, and nothing in this body ever sets it. A dirty/valid flag is the obvious reading and is not claimed; the sibling entries of the table at 0x013f69b4 (0x005a2050, 0x005a2320) may write it and would be the place to look.

The fifteen key ids have no preimages. They are 32-bit hashed names and this package has no table that maps them, so none of the twenty-one stored quantities is named. The id-to-displacement map in mechanics.receiver_displacement is the most this body alone can fix.

The class of the parameter object is unknown, so the model's three slot declarations carry only the three slot displacements and the two argument shapes. Whether the +0x1c and +0x28 slots are the same member under two names, whether the +0x24 slot's out-parameter is a pointer-to-pointer or a pointer to a small struct, and what the +0x24 slot returns in EAX, are all unestablished. The body never reads EAX after a +0x24 call, so the model's slot returns bool from the caller's point of view and the rest of the callee's return word is ignored, which is faithful and is not a claim about the callee.

Whether the record the +0x24 slot hands back is the same object as the one the +0x28 slot would return for the same key is not established. This body never asks the +0x28 slot for 0x01102b20 or 0x01102b2f, so the two paths never meet in this body and nothing here compares them.

The two reciprocals at 0x013f6960 and 0x013f6964 are 0.01745329238474369f and 57.295780181884766f and sit in a four-word .rdata run with e and pi. That is why this package is willing to call them the degrees-to-radians and radians-to-degrees constants: the values are the reciprocals of each other to the last bit and of pi/180 to 23 bits. No record in this repository names them, and no record establishes that the twenty-one quantities they scale are angles; the model applies the multiply where the listing puts it and says nothing about what the values mean.

The type tag 0x10 is read as a float here, on the same footing as 0xd, and the two +0x24 blocks reject it while the twelve inline blocks accept it. That asymmetry is in the bytes. Whether 0x10 is a string tag that the inline copies happen to reinterpret as a float, or a second numeric tag, is not established, and it is the sharpest behavioural difference between the two block shapes in the body.
